questions.p: Because 'our class teacher' dey explain who Mrs. Adeyemi be, you must put comma for front and back. If you no do am like that, the sentence no go balance.

questions.q: Choose the option with the correct spelling of the word that means 'a person who studies and treats diseases of the mind'.
questions.e: The correct spelling is psychologist, beginning with the silent 'p' before 'sy' and followed by 'ch'. The other forms either drop the silent p or misorder the letters.
questions.p: The correct spelling start with silent 'p' then 'sychologist'. Any other way you write am, you don miss the correct spelling.

questions.q: Choose the option that correctly uses the apostrophe.
o: The children's toys were scattered all over the sitting room.
The childrens's toys were scattered all over the sitting room.
The childrens toys were scattered all over the sitting room.
The childrens' toys were scattered all over the sitting room.
questions.e: Children is already plural, so possession is shown by adding apostrophe + s, giving 'children's'. Adding just an apostrophe after the s, or no apostrophe at all, is wrong because 'childrens' is not a real plural form.
questions.p: Children na plural already, so to show say something belong to them, you go add apostrophe and 's'. 'Childrens' no be correct English at all.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated version of the following sentence: Chidi asked his brother if he had collected the WAEC result slip
o: Chidi asked his brother if he had collected the WAEC result slip?
Chidi asked his brother, "if he had collected the WAEC result slip"?
Chidi asked his brother if he had collected the WAEC result slip.
Chidi asked, "his brother if he had collected the WAEC result slip."
questions.e: This is a reported (indirect) question, so it ends with a full stop, not a question mark, and needs no quotation marks since no exact words are quoted. The other options wrongly add quotation marks or a question mark to a statement that merely reports a question.
questions.p: Because na indirect question, you no need quotation mark or question mark. Just put full stop for the end because you dey report wetin person talk.

questions.q: Choose the option in which the word is correctly spelt.
questions.e: The correct British spelling is 'manoeuvre', keeping the 'oeu' sequence intact. The distractors rearrange or drop letters from this unusual vowel combination.
questions.p: The correct British spelling na 'manoeuvre'. Any other way you arrange the letters, e go be mistake.

questions.q:
Chief Okoro, a wealthy farmer from Abia State, kept three things close to his heart: his family, his farmland, and his faith. Every morning before going to his cassava farm, he would gather his children and remind them that hard work, patience, and honesty were the keys to a good life. His neighbours often sought his advice on both farming and family matters.
Which of the following sentences about Chief Okoro is correctly punctuated according to the passage's style of listing three items?
o: He valued honesty, loyalty and courage, above wealth.
He valued honesty loyalty and courage above wealth.
He valued honesty; loyalty; and courage above wealth.
He valued honesty, loyalty, and courage above wealth.
questions.e: In a list of three items, commas should separate each item, including before 'and' (the Oxford comma style used in the passage), with no comma before 'above wealth'. The other options either miss commas entirely or wrongly use semicolons or a stray comma.
questions.p: When you dey list three things, you must use comma to separate them, even before the 'and'. No put comma for where e no suppose dey.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'the act of giving up a throne or position of power'.
questions.e: The correct word is 'abdication', formed from 'abdicate' plus the suffix '-ion'. The other options wrongly double the consonant, change the vowel or misspell the ending.
questions.p: Na 'abdication' be the correct spelling, wey come from 'abdicate' join with '-ion'. Di other options just double wrong letter or spell am anyhow.

questions.q: In an examination hall in Minna, Fatima was asked to identify the correctly spelt word from a set that tests silent letters. Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.e: The word 'pneumatic' begins with a silent 'p' before 'n' and has one 't'. Candidates often drop the silent letter or wrongly double the final consonant, which the other options show.
questions.p: Na 'pneumatic' correct because e get silent 'p' for front and one 't' for back. Di other options remove di silent 'p' or double letter where dem no suppose to.

questions.q: Choose the option that correctly uses the colon.
o: The coach named four players: Tunde, Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
The coach named: four players, Tunde, Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
The coach named four players, Tunde: Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
The coach named four players Tunde: Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
questions.e: A colon correctly introduces a list after a complete independent clause, as seen when it follows 'four players'. The other options place the colon in the middle of the clause or list, which breaks the grammar.
questions.p: Na option A correct because colon suppose come after full sentence before you list something. Di other options put di colon for wrong place wey scatter grammar.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated version of the following sentence: Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday however her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
o: Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday; however, her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday, however her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday however, her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
Mrs Adebayo said, that she would travel to Kano on Friday; however her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
questions.e: Two independent clauses joined by the conjunctive adverb 'however' need a semicolon before it and a comma after it. The other options use only a comma before 'however', which creates a comma splice, or add an unnecessary comma elsewhere.
questions.p: Na option A correct because when two strong sentence join with 'however', you must put semicolon before am and comma after am. Di other options make mistake with comma.

questions.q: In normal educated speech, three of the following words have the same vowel sound while one is different. Identify the ODD ONE OUT.
questions.e: COAT, BOAT and GOAT all have the diphthong /əʊ/. GOT, however, has the short vowel sound /ɒ/, which is different from the others.
questions.p: COAT, BOAT and GOAT dey share di same diphthong sound /əʊ/. But GOT get short vowel sound /ɒ/, wey make am different from di rest.

questions.q: Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
questions.e: PHOTOGRAPH is a three-syllable noun that is stressed on the first syllable: PHO-to-graph. This is different from PHOTOGRAPHY, which shifts stress to the second syllable.
questions.p: PHOTOGRAPH na three-syllable noun wey dey carry stress for di first syllable, PHO-to-graph. E dey different from PHOTOGRAPHY wey dey carry im own stress for di second syllable.

questions.q: The word ENGINEER can function as a noun. Choose the option with the correct stress pattern for this word.
questions.e: ENGINEER is stressed on the last syllable: en-gi-NEER. Many three-syllable words ending in -eer or -ain take the stress on the final syllable, unlike most English nouns which prefer front stress.
questions.p: ENGINEER dey carry stress for di last syllable, en-gi-NEER. Plenty three-syllable words wey dey end with -eer or -ain dey carry stress for di back, unlike normal English nouns.

questions.q: Four students were asked to pronounce the word CHARACTERISTIC and each gave a different stress pattern. Choose the option with the correct stress pattern.
questions.e: CHARACTERISTIC is stressed on the fourth syllable: cha-rac-ter-IS-tic. Long words formed from a shorter root (CHARACTER) often shift their stress closer to the ending, especially before suffixes like -istic.
questions.p: CHARACTERISTIC dey carry stress for di fourth syllable, cha-rac-ter-IS-tic. Long words wey come from short root like CHARACTER dey shift dia stress go back, especially before suffix like -istic.

questions.q: In Nigerian secondary schools, students are often tested on the stress pattern of the word PRESENT, which can function as either a noun or a verb. Choose the option that shows the CORRECT stress pattern when PRESENT means a gift given to someone.
questions.e: When PRESENT is used as a noun meaning a gift, the stress falls on the first syllable. If it were used as a verb meaning to give or show something, the stress would shift to the second syllable instead.
questions.p: If you wan talk say person give you gift, you go stress the first part of the word. But if you wan talk say you dey show person something, the stress go move go the second part.

questions.q: Four WAEC examiners disagreed on how to stress the word NECESSARY during a marking workshop. Choose the word with the correct stress pattern.
questions.e: NECESSARY is stressed on the first syllable, even though it has four syllables. Many candidates wrongly place stress on the second syllable because of the strong middle sound, but standard pronunciation keeps the stress at the front.
questions.p: For this word, the correct stress dey for the first syllable. Many people dey make mistake put am for the middle, but that one no correct.

questions.q: The word INCREASE can be used as both a noun and a verb in English, and its stress pattern changes with its grammatical function. Choose the option with the CORRECT stress pattern for INCREASE when it functions as a verb meaning to become greater.
questions.e: As a verb, INCREASE is stressed on the second syllable, while as a noun it is stressed on the first syllable. This noun-verb stress shift is common in many two-syllable English words such as CONTRACT and RECORD.
questions.p: When you use this word as verb, the stress must dey for the second syllable. If na noun you dey use, the stress go come back for the first one.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the most appropriate answer.

The governor will commission the new bridge NEXT WEEK.
o: When will the governor commission the new bridge?
What will the governor commission next week?
Why will the governor commission the new bridge?
Who will commission the new bridge?
questions.e: NEXT WEEK tells us the time of the action, so the sentence answers a question asking when the event will happen. The other questions focus on the object, the doer, or the reason, not the time.
questions.p: NEXT WEEK dey show us when di action happen, na im make di sentence answer question wey ask about time. Di other questions dey talk about wetin, who, or why, not time.

questions.q:
Choose the question which the given sentence is the appropriate answer to, with emphasis on the capitalized word.

Mr. Afolabi repaired the generator WITH A SPANNER.
o: How did Mr. Afolabi repair the generator?
Where did Mr. Afolabi repair the generator?
questions.e: WITH A SPANNER describes the instrument or manner used to carry out the repair, so the sentence answers a question about how the action was done. It does not tell us the place, the doer, or the object repaired.
questions.p: WITH A SPANNER dey explain how Mr. Afolabi take repair di generator. Na im make di sentence answer question wey ask how di work happen.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the most appropriate answer.

It was the LIBRARIAN, not the student, who locked the reading room.
o: When did the librarian lock the reading room?
Why did the librarian lock the reading room?
questions.e: The cleft structure 'It was the LIBRARIAN who...' places emphatic stress on the doer of the action, correcting a possible assumption that it was the student. This directly answers a question about who performed the action.
questions.p: Di sentence put emphasis on di person wey lock di room, wey be di LIBRARIAN. Na im make am answer question about who do di work.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the most appropriate answer.

Adaeze travels to Enugu EVERY TWO WEEKS to see her grandmother.
o: How often does Adaeze travel to Enugu?
Why does Adaeze travel to Enugu?
Who does Adaeze travel to Enugu to see?
Where does Adaeze travel to see her grandmother?
questions.e: EVERY TWO WEEKS shows the frequency of the trips, so the sentence answers a question about how often Adaeze travels. It does not explain the destination, the reason, or the person being visited.
questions.p: EVERY TWO WEEKS dey show how frequent Adaeze dey travel. Na im make di sentence answer question wey ask how often she dey go.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the most appropriate answer.

The committee rejected the proposal BECAUSE OF ITS HIGH COST.
o: When did the committee reject the proposal?
Why did the committee reject the proposal?
questions.e: BECAUSE OF ITS HIGH COST gives the reason for the committee's decision, so it answers a question asking why the proposal was rejected. The other options ask about the object, the doer, or the time, none of which is stressed here.
questions.p: BECAUSE OF ITS HIGH COST dey give reason why committee reject di proposal. Na im make am answer question wey ask why.

questions.q:
Choose the question which the given sentence is the appropriate answer to, with emphasis on the capitalized word.

The twins did not merely pass the examination; they EXCELLED in it.
o: What did the twins do in the examination?
Why did the twins excel in the examination?
When did the twins excel in the examination?
questions.e: The contrast 'not merely pass... but EXCELLED' stresses the manner or degree of their performance, so the sentence answers what exactly the twins did in the exam, beyond simply passing. It is not asking for the time, the doer, or a reason, since those are already known from the context.
questions.p: Di sentence show how well di twins perform for di exam pass ordinary pass. Na im make am answer wetin dem do for inside di exam.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the most appropriate answer.

Mallam Sule sold the cattle to the TRADER FROM KANO, and not to any buyer from Lagos.
o: When did Mallam Sule sell the cattle?
Who did Mallam Sule sell the cattle to?
Where did Mallam Sule sell the cattle?
questions.e: The phrase 'and not to any buyer from Lagos' shows that the emphasis is on identifying the particular buyer, the TRADER FROM KANO, so the sentence answers a question about who received the cattle. The sale item, place, and time are not in focus here.
questions.p: Di sentence make am clear say na di TRADER FROM KANO buy di cattle. Na im make am answer question about who Mallam Sule sell cattle give.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the appropriate answer.

"Mrs. Adebayo cooked the JOLLOF rice for the party."
o: Why did Mrs. Adebayo cook jollof rice for the party?
Who cooked the jollof rice for the party?
Did Mrs. Adebayo cook the jollof rice well?
What did Mrs. Adebayo cook for the party?
questions.e: The stress is on JOLLOF, which tells us the item cooked is being singled out. This answers a question asking what was cooked, not who cooked it or why.
questions.p: Na JOLLOF wey carry the stress dey show say na that particular food wey she cook dem dey ask for. E dey answer question wey ask wetin she cook, no be who cook am.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the appropriate answer.

"It was CHIOMA who reported the broken generator to the hostel warden."
o: What did Chioma report to the warden?
To whom did Chioma report the broken generator?
Who reported the broken generator to the warden?
Why did Chioma report the broken generator?
questions.e: The cleft structure "It was CHIOMA who..." places stress on the person who performed the action. This construction directly answers a question asking who did the reporting.
questions.p: As CHIOMA get stress for head like that, na to point out the person wey do the work. E straight answer question wey dey find who report the generator.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the appropriate answer.

"The students passed the examination because they STUDIED hard, not because the paper was easy."
o: Why did the students pass the examination?
What examination did the students pass?
How long did the students study for the examination?
questions.e: The stressed word STUDIED, together with the contrast clause rejecting an easy paper as the reason, shows the sentence is giving a cause. This fits a question asking why the students passed.
questions.p: The stress wey dey STUDIED dey tell us the reason why dem pass the exam. Naim make the sentence answer question wey ask why dem pass.

questions.q:
In the sentence below, the word in capitals carries emphatic stress. Choose the question to which the sentence is the appropriate answer.

"The committee members voted AGAINST the new tuition policy during the meeting."
o: How did the committee members vote on the policy?
Who voted against the new tuition policy?
What did the committee members vote on?
When did the committee members vote?
questions.e: The stress on AGAINST shows the manner or direction of the vote is being emphasised, not the topic or the people involved. This matches a question asking how they voted.
questions.p: If AGAINST carry stress, e mean say na how dem vote dem dey explain, no be the matter wey dem vote for. Naim make am answer question wey ask how dem vote.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: If Ngozi had studied harder, she _____ the scholarship examination last year.
questions.e: This is a third conditional referring to an unreal past situation. The structure requires 'would have + past participle' in the main clause, hence 'would have passed'.
questions.p: Dis na third conditional wey dey talk about something wey no happen for past. E need 'would have + past participle', so 'would have passed' correct.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the same meaning as the sentence in quotes: Adamu said, 'I am travelling to Kano tomorrow.'
o: Adamu said that he is travelling to Kano tomorrow.
Adamu said that he will be travelling to Kano the following day.
Adamu said that he was travelling to Kano the next day.
Adamu says that he was travelling to Kano tomorrow.
questions.e: In reported speech, the present continuous tense changes to past continuous, and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' since the reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense.
questions.p: For reported speech, present continuous dey turn to past continuous, and 'tomorrow' dey change to 'the next day' because 'said' dey past tense.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: _____ the final examination results late, the students would have organized a peaceful protest.
questions.e: This is an inverted third conditional in which 'if' is omitted and the auxiliary 'had' is placed before the subject. The correct inverted form is 'Had the school released', matching the result clause 'would have organized'.
questions.p: Na inverted third conditional be dis where we remove 'if' and put 'had' before the subject. 'Had the school released' na the correct one.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the sentence in quotes in the passive voice: 'The governor is constructing three new flyovers in the state capital.'
o: Three new flyovers are constructed by the governor in the state capital.
Three new flyovers are being constructed by the governor in the state capital.
Three new flyovers have been constructed by the governor in the state capital.
Three new flyovers were being constructed by the governor in the state capital.
questions.e: The original sentence is in the present continuous active tense, so the passive form must also be present continuous: 'am/is/are being + past participle'. This gives 'are being constructed'.
questions.p: Since the original sentence dey present continuous active, the passive must be present continuous too. Na 'are being constructed' be the correct answer.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the same meaning as the sentence in quotes: The coach asked the players, 'Have you completed your training for today?'
o: The coach asked the players if they completed their training for that day.
The coach asked the players had they completed their training for today.
The coach asked the players if they have completed their training for today.
The coach asked the players whether they had completed their training for that day.
questions.e: A reported yes/no question requires 'if' or 'whether', a statement word order, and the present perfect tense shifting back to past perfect. 'Today' also changes to 'that day'.
questions.p: For reported yes/no question, you must use 'if' or 'whether', arrange the sentence well, and change present perfect to past perfect. 'Today' con turn to 'that day'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Were the government to fix the Benin-Ore road, commuters _____ fewer accidents on that route.
questions.e: This is an inverted second conditional expressing a present or future unreal situation, using 'Were...to' instead of 'If'. The main clause therefore takes 'would + base verb', which is 'would experience'.
questions.p: Dis na second conditional wey use 'Were...to' instead of 'if' for unreal situation. The main clause suppose take 'would + base verb', wey be 'would experience'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: If the WAEC officials _____ the examination timetable earlier, candidates would have prepared adequately.
questions.e: This is a third conditional about an unreal past situation. The if-clause needs the past perfect 'had released', and the main clause correctly uses 'would have prepared'.
questions.p: Dis na third conditional for matter wey don pass before. Na 'had released' suppose enter di if-clause to match 'would have prepared'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the sentence in quotes in the passive voice: "Someone has stolen the chairman's official car from the car park."
o: The chairman's official car has been stolen from the car park.
The chairman's official car had been stolen from the car park.
The chairman's official car is being stolen from the car park.
The chairman's official car was stolen from the car park.
questions.e: The active sentence is in the present perfect tense, so the passive form must also be present perfect: 'has been stolen'. The agent 'someone' is dropped since it is not important.
questions.p: Di original sentence dey inside present perfect tense, so di passive version must still use 'has been stolen'. We no need put 'someone' again for inside.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: _____ I to win this scholarship, I would dedicate it to my late father's memory.
questions.e: This is an inverted conditional sentence expressing a hypothetical future situation, formed by inverting 'were' with the subject instead of using 'if'. The correct inverted form is 'Were I to win', which means 'If I were to win'.
questions.p: Dis one na inverted conditional wey talk about future wey never happen. Instead of 'if', we go use 'Were I to win' to make am correct.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the same meaning as the sentence in quotes: The invigilator said, 'Stop writing immediately and drop your pens.'
o: The invigilator asked if the candidates could stop writing immediately and drop their pens.
The invigilator said that the candidates should stop writing immediately and drop their pens.
The invigilator ordered the candidates to stop writing immediately and drop their pens.
The invigilator suggested that the candidates stop writing immediately and drop their pens.
questions.e: The original sentence is a command given with a firm, authoritative tone, so the correct reporting verb is 'ordered', followed by the infinitive form 'to stop'. This best captures the imperative force of the original statement.
questions.p: Na strong command di invigilator give, so 'ordered' plus 'to stop' be di correct way to report am. E show authority well well.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Provided that the contractors _____ the bridge before the rainy season, the villagers will cross the river safely.
questions.e: 'Provided that' functions like 'if' in a first conditional sentence, so the condition clause takes the simple present tense 'complete', while the main clause uses the future tense 'will cross'. Mixing tenses like 'will complete' in the condition clause is a common error to avoid.
questions.p: Because 'Provided that' dey like 'if' for first conditional, na simple present tense 'complete' we need for di condition. We no suppose use 'will complete'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the sentence in quotes in the passive voice: "By next year, the government will have built ten new hospitals across the state."
o: Ten new hospitals will have been built across the state by next year.
Ten new hospitals are being built across the state by next year.
Ten new hospitals will be built across the state by the government by next year.
Ten new hospitals would have been built across the state by next year.
questions.e: The active sentence is in the future perfect tense, so the passive equivalent must also be future perfect: 'will have been built'. The agent 'by the government' can be omitted since the focus is on the hospitals, not who builds them.
questions.p: Di active sentence dey for future perfect tense, so di passive must be 'will have been built'. We fitot remove 'by the government' make di sentence sweet.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Because the midfielder had already received a yellow card earlier in the match, the referee's second caution resulted in a _____.
questions.e: In football register, a second yellow card automatically becomes a red card, which sends the player off the pitch. The other terms describe unrelated match restarts.
questions.p: For football matter, once player collect two yellow card, e must turn to red card and the referee go send am comot for field. Na only red card dey show say person don collect second yellow.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: In banking usage, the document that instructs a bank to pay a stated sum from one's account to a named person is called a _____.
questions.e: A cheque is the standard banking instrument used to order payment from an account holder's funds to another party. A receipt and invoice merely record transactions, while a voucher supports accounting entries.
questions.p: Na cheque dem dey use tell bank make dem pay money from person account give another person. Receipt and invoice na just paper for record, but na cheque be correct instruction for payment.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: During the land dispute hearing, the judge asked both parties to present their _____ before he could give a ruling.
questions.e: Testimonies are statements given by parties or witnesses before a judgement is reached. A verdict and sentence come after the judge has decided, while an indictment is a formal criminal charge, not evidence from parties.
questions.p: Before judge go give judgment, both people must bring their testimonies to show wetin happen. Na after everything judge go come give verdict, no be before the case start.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The athlete was disqualified from the 100-metre race for committing a _____, having left the blocks before the gun was fired.
questions.e: A false start occurs when a sprinter moves before the starting gun, leading to disqualification in track events. Foul throw, handball and offside belong to other sports such as football and are not relevant here.
questions.p: If runner move for starting block before gun shoot, dem dey call am false start and na im make dem disqualify the person. The other options no concern 100-metre race at all.

questions.q: Read the passage and answer the question that follows: Funmilayo took her late father's estate to court after her stepbrothers claimed sole ownership of the family house. The judge examined the will tendered as evidence and ruled that the property be shared equally among all the children. Funmilayo's lawyer later explained that the ruling had settled the matter permanently, and no party could reopen the case on the same grounds. Which legal term best describes the lawyer's explanation of the ruling's effect?
questions.e: Since the lawyer says the matter is settled permanently and cannot be reopened on the same grounds, this describes a ruling that is final and binding. The other options all suggest the case could still change, which contradicts the passage.
questions.p: Because the lawyer talk say case don finish permanently and nobody fit bring am back again, e mean say judgment don final and binding. E no dey subject to appeal again.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: A customer who wishes to transfer money regularly to pay a fixed bill, such as rent, without visiting the bank each time, should set up a _____.
questions.e: A standing order is a banking instruction that automatically makes fixed, regular payments from a customer's account. A bank statement only records transactions, a loan facility provides borrowed funds, and an overdraft permits spending beyond the account balance.
questions.p: If you wan make bank dey pay fixed money like rent every time without stress, na standing order you go setup. E go dey send the money automatically.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: In sporting register, a team that fails to field enough players for a scheduled match may be made to forfeit the game by a _____.
questions.e: A walkover is awarded when an opponent is unable or unwilling to play, so the other team wins automatically. Handicap, knockout and playoff describe different competition arrangements.
questions.p: Dem dey give walkover when anoda team no show or no fit play match, so di oda team go just win straight. Di oda words like handicap, knockout and playoff na different tin for sports.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Before a company can be listed on the stock exchange, its shares must first be offered to the public through an _____.
questions.e: An initial public offer is the process by which a company first sells shares to the public to be listed on the exchange. The other terms belong to banking or legal usage and do not describe this process.
questions.p: Initial public offer na di way wey company dey use sell dia share to everybody for first time before dem put am for market. Di oda words na bank or court matter, e no concern dis one.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: In medical register, the process of examining a patient to find out the nature of an illness before treatment begins is known as _____.
questions.e: Diagnosis is the identification of an illness through examination. Prognosis predicts the likely course of the disease, therapy is treatment, and dosage is the measured amount of medicine given.
questions.p: Diagnosis na when doctor check patient well well to know weda sickness dey body before treatment start. Prognosis dey talk how sickness fit be later, therapy na treatment, and dosage na di amount of medicine.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: During the cup final, the referee allowed three extra minutes of _____ time to make up for stoppages caused by injuries.
questions.e: Added time, also called stoppage time, is played at the end of a half to compensate for time lost to injuries or delays. Half, extra and full time describe other divisions of a match and do not fit this sporting usage.
questions.p: Added time, wey dem still dey call stoppage time, na di extra minutes wey referee dey add for end of match to cover time wey waste for injury. Di oda words no mean dis sports style at all.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: When Adaeze's current account was wrongly debited twice for the same transaction, she visited her bank to formally request a _____ of the extra charge.
questions.e: A reversal cancels a wrong debit and returns the money to the customer's account, which is what Adaeze needed. Overdraft, collateral and liquidation refer to unrelated banking concepts.
questions.p: Reversal na when bank cancel wrong money wey dem remove from account and return am to owner, na im Adaeze go find. Overdraft, collateral and liquidation na different bank grammar.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Counsel for the defence raised an _____ to the admission of the document, arguing that it had been obtained unlawfully.
questions.e: An objection is a formal protest raised by a lawyer against evidence or procedure during a trial, which fits the scenario of challenging the document's admission. An affidavit is a sworn statement, an adjournment postpones proceedings, and an indictment formally charges someone with a crime, none of which match raising a protest against evidence.
questions.p: Objection na when lawyer shout for court say make dem no take evidence because dem pack am through illegal way. Affidavit, adjournment and indictment get dia own different meaning for law.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

Most Nigerian farmers still depend on rainfall for their crops. When the rains fail or come late, the harvest suffers and food prices rise. Agricultural experts have long advised that irrigation schemes be built across the country to reduce this dependence on the weather. Yet, many of these schemes remain uncompleted years after they were started, while farmers continue to watch the sky with anxiety each planting season.

What is the writer's attitude towards the state of irrigation schemes in the passage?
o: Indifferent, since the farmers' situation does not concern him
Amused by the farmers' continued reliance on rainfall
Optimistic, believing the schemes will soon be completed
Disapproving, because the schemes have been neglected despite their importance
questions.e: The writer points out that the schemes remain uncompleted years after starting, which shows disapproval of the neglect. There is no hint of indifference, optimism, or amusement in the tone.
questions.p: Di writer no happy sake of say di irrigation projects never finish after so many years. E show say e no like how dem neglect di work even though e dey important for farmers.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

In many Nigerian markets, bargaining is not merely about reducing price; it is a social ritual that builds relationships between buyer and seller. A buyer who refuses to haggle may be seen as proud or unfriendly, while one who bargains skilfully often earns the trader's respect and sometimes a discount beyond the agreed price.

What does the word RITUAL mean as used in the passage?
o: A religious ceremony performed in the market
A customary practice carried out in a particular way
A secret agreement between two people
questions.e: In this context, ritual refers to a customary social practice, bargaining, that is regularly carried out in a set manner. It is not about religion, rarity, or secrecy here.
questions.p: For dis passage, ritual mean di way pipo dey do tins as custom for market. E no mean say na religion or secret tin, na just how dem dey bargain for price.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

When Ngozi resigned from her well-paid banking job to start a small bakery, many of her relatives thought she had lost her senses. Her father reminded her, almost daily, of the comfort she was giving up. Yet Ngozi had grown tired of spending long hours producing reports that were read by no one and decisions that were never hers to make. She wanted work that let her see, at the end of each day, something she had actually built with her own hands. Three years on, her bakery supplies bread to two schools in her neighbourhood, and she has never once regretted her choice.

What is the main reason Ngozi gave up her banking job?
o: Her father insisted that she should start a business instead
She wanted work that gave her a visible, personal sense of achievement
She discovered that baking was far more profitable than banking
The bank refused to increase her salary after many years of service
questions.e: The passage says she was tired of work whose results she never saw and wanted to build something with her own hands. There is no mention of pay comparison or her father forcing a business idea; in fact he was against her decision.
questions.p: Na true. Di passage tok sey Ngozi tire to dey do work wey she no dey see di result, and she want build somtin wit 'am by herself. Her papa even against am.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

The old clock tower at the centre of the town had stopped working for so long that younger residents assumed it was merely a decoration. Its hands, frozen at a quarter past three, had become a kind of joke among commuters who used it only as a meeting point, never as a timepiece. When a visiting engineer offered, free of charge, to repair it, the town council politely declined, explaining that the clock's silence had itself become a landmark of sorts, one the people had grown fond of and were unwilling to disturb.

What can be inferred about the town council's attitude towards the broken clock?
o: They valued the clock's familiar, unchanging presence over its usefulness
They planned to replace the clock with a modern digital one soon
They did not believe the engineer was skilled enough to fix it
They were too poor to pay the engineer for his services
questions.e: The council refused a free repair because the clock's stillness had become a cherished landmark, showing they preferred its familiar state to having it work. The passage states the offer was free, so cost was not the issue, and nothing suggests doubt about the engineer's skill or any replacement plan.
questions.p: E correct. Di council refuse free repair because dem like di clock as landmark wey don stay long. Money no be di problem, and nobody doubt di engineer.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

Critics of the new examination policy argue that reducing the number of subjects a student may register for will narrow young people's intellectual horizons. Supporters counter that the previous system, which allowed candidates to sit for as many as nine subjects, encouraged shallow, rushed preparation rather than deep understanding. The policy's framers insist that a student who masters six subjects thoroughly is better equipped for further studies than one who merely scratches the surface of nine. Whether this trade-off between breadth and depth will truly benefit learners remains to be seen in the coming years.

What is the writer's attitude towards the new examination policy?
o: Cautiously uncertain, presenting both sides without taking a firm position
Strongly supportive, praising the policy as an obvious improvement
Deeply hostile, condemning the policymakers as careless
Indifferent, showing no interest in the debate at all
questions.e: The writer presents both the critics' and supporters' views fairly and ends by saying the outcome remains to be seen, showing balanced uncertainty rather than clear support or opposition. There is no sign of hostility or indifference, since the writer engages seriously with the arguments on both sides.
questions.p: Na correct. Di writer show wetin both critics and supporters dey talk and come yarn sey make we wait see di outcome. E no take any side.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

Temitope had always believed that hard work alone guaranteed success, until she watched her less diligent cousin secure a scholarship through a chance meeting with a visiting professor. The incident did not make her stop working hard, but it did soften a conviction that had once been absolute. She began to accept that effort mattered greatly, yet was not the only thread in the fabric of achievement; opportunity, timing and even luck played their quiet parts as well.

What does the passage suggest Temitope came to understand?
o: Scholarships are usually awarded unfairly to undeserving students
Hard work no longer has any value in achieving success
Success depends on more than hard work alone
Her cousin did not deserve the scholarship she received
questions.e: The passage shows Temitope moving from believing hard work alone guarantees success to accepting that opportunity and luck also matter. It does not say hard work is worthless, nor does it judge her cousin as undeserving or claim scholarships are generally unfair.
questions.p: E correct. Temitope come realize sey apart from hard work, luck and opportunity dey play major role for success. E no mean sey hard work useless.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

A new by-law in a certain town requires that every commercial motorcyclist wear a reflective jacket after sunset. Enforcement officers have been stationed at major junctions to issue fines to defaulters. Within weeks, accident reports involving motorcyclists at night fell noticeably, a development the town's traffic authority has celebrated as proof that the measure works. Some riders, however, complain that the jackets are uncomfortable in the heat and that the real cause of night accidents is poor street lighting, not invisibility.

What is the meaning of the word DEFAULTERS as used in the passage?
o: Those who design the reflective jackets for riders
Those who fail to comply with the required rule
Those who report accidents to the traffic authority
Those who patrol the junctions to enforce the law
questions.e: In the passage, defaulters are the motorcyclists who do not wear the reflective jackets as the by-law demands, and so are fined. The word refers to rule-breakers, not to the officers who enforce the law or report accidents.
questions.p: Na so. Defaulters na di people wey no gree follow di new rule to wear reflective jacket, na dat one make dem fine dem.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

Although the lecturer's voice rarely rose above a murmur, his classroom was always the quietest and most attentive in the faculty. Students who struggled to stay awake in louder, more animated lectures elsewhere found themselves leaning forward to catch his every word. He never repeated a sentence twice, as though daring his audience to listen the first time or lose the thread entirely. Many later admitted that this unusual discipline taught them more about careful listening than any other course they took.

What can be inferred about the effect of the lecturer's teaching style on his students?
o: It encouraged them to record his lectures instead of listening directly
It frustrated them so much that most eventually stopped attending
It made the course content easier to understand than other courses
It trained them to listen with unusual care and attention
questions.e: The passage shows that his refusal to repeat himself forced students to listen closely, and many later said it taught them careful listening skills. There is no mention of frustration causing absence, easier content, or recording devices, so these are not supported.
questions.p: E correct. Because di lecturer no dey repeat wetin 'e talk, students come learn how to dey listen well well with deep attention.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

The committee tasked with renaming the community hall spent four long meetings debating a single word. Some members wanted a name honouring the town's founder, while others preferred something that reflected the hall's modern use as a venue for weddings and conferences. After much argument, a quiet compromise emerged: the hall would bear the founder's name, followed by a simple word describing its function. Nobody left the final meeting entirely satisfied, but nobody left angry either, and the matter was finally laid to rest.

What does the phrase LAID TO REST mean as used in the passage?
questions.e: In this context, laid to rest means the long-running debate over the hall's name was finally settled through compromise. It does not refer to an actual burial, nor does it mean the matter was postponed or forgotten, since a decision was clearly reached.
questions.p: Na true. To 'lay to rest' for dis matter mean sey dem don finally settle di argument and reach conclusion. E no mean say dem bury anytin.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

In the small fishing settlement, elders tell newcomers never to mock the river aloud, for it is said to answer insults with sudden, unexplained misfortune. Younger, formally educated residents dismiss this as pure superstition, yet even they lower their voices and choose their words carefully whenever they cross the river by canoe. Asked why they bother with a belief they claim not to hold, one young man shrugged and said simply that there was no harm in being careful, just in case the old stories held some grain of truth after all.

What does the passage suggest about the young man's real attitude towards the belief?
o: He is unaware of the belief and acts out of pure habit alone
He is entirely convinced the belief is false and acts without any caution
He fully believes the old stories and fears the river's power completely
He is privately uncertain and takes a cautious approach despite his claimed disbelief
questions.e: Although the young man claims not to believe the superstition, his careful behaviour and his remark about being careful just in case reveal a hidden uncertainty. This shows he is neither a full believer nor a complete disbeliever acting without caution.
questions.p: E correct. Even though di young man say e no believe di juju, e still dey careful just in case di story na true. E get small fear for mind.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fills the gap.

The chairman of the community meeting raised his hand to ___ order after the youths had argued for almost an hour without reaching any agreement.
questions.e: To restore order is the standard collocation meaning to bring back peace or calm after confusion. Return and recover do not collocate naturally with order, and revive suggests bringing something back to life, which does not fit.
questions.p: Na 'restore' be the correct word to use with 'order' when pesin wan bring back peace after argument. Di other words no gel with order at all.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fills the gap.

Mr. Bello warned his students that anyone caught cheating during the mock examination would be dealt with ___ the school's disciplinary code demands.
questions.e: As is used here as a conjunction introducing a clause of manner, meaning 'in the way that'. Like should not introduce a full clause in formal usage, while so and such do not fit this grammatical slot.
questions.p: Na 'as' dem suppose use here because e dey show how something happen according to rule. 'Like' no fit follow full sentence for formal grammar.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the option that best fills the gap.

Despite the heavy downpour that flooded most streets in Lagos that morning, Chinedu still arrived at the office early; ___, his colleague who lived nearby came in late because he had overslept.
questions.e: Ironically fits because it is surprising that the colleague living nearby, who should have had an easier journey, arrived late while Chinedu, who faced the flood, came early. Consequently and similarly do not capture this contrast, and undoubtedly does not express irony.
questions.p: Na 'ironically' correct because e shock everybody as di person wey stay near come late, while di person wey face flood come early.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the option that best fills the gap.

By the time the WAEC results were finally released, Tunde ___ for admission into three different universities, hoping that at least one would accept him.
questions.e: Had applied is correct because the action of applying was completed before another past time, the release of the results, showing the past perfect tense. The other options do not correctly show an action finished before a later past event.
questions.p: Na 'had applied' correct because di application happen and finish before results come out for past. E show past perfect tense well well.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fills the gap.

The young trader was so ___ in his business dealings that even customers who had been cheated elsewhere trusted him completely.
questions.e: Honest best explains why customers who had been cheated before would trust the trader completely, since trust usually follows honesty. Generous, wealthy and popular do not directly connect to earning trust in business dealings.
questions.p: Na 'honest' fit dis place pass because na person wey dey truthful people dey trust for business. Di other options no mean say person go trust am.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the option that best fills the gap.

The new supervisor at the textile factory in Kano was known for his firmness. He insisted that every worker ___ to the safety rules, no matter how senior they were, because he believed accidents could be prevented through discipline.
questions.e: The verb 'insisted that' introduces a subjunctive mood, which requires the base form of the verb regardless of subject. Therefore 'adhere' is correct, not the inflected forms.
questions.p: Dis one na subjunctive mood, where pesin must use di base verb 'adhere' afta 'insisted that', no matter who dem dey talk about.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fills the gap.

The twins, Kemi and Kunle, were inseparable from childhood. Wherever one went, the other followed, so much so that their classmates nicknamed them ___ peas in a pod.
questions.e: The idiom 'like two peas in a pod' describes people who are very similar or always together. The other options do not form a correct or recognised expression.
questions.p: Di correct idiom wey dem dey use to describe people wey dey always move togeda na 'like two peas in a pod'.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the option that best fills the gap.

The village elders gathered under the old baobab tree to settle the land dispute between the two families. ___ hours of argument, they reached a compromise that satisfied both sides, and the matter was finally laid to rest.
questions.e: The sentence describes a sequence of events: the arguing happened first, and the compromise came afterwards. 'After' correctly shows this time relationship, while the other words either suggest an ongoing simultaneous action or a wrong time frame.
questions.p: Na 'After' dem suppose use becos di argument happen first before dem reach compromise. E show di correct time sequence.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fills the gap.

The young intern was eager to impress her new employer. On her first day, she arrived an hour early and stayed late, determined to prove that she was ___ of the responsibility given to her.
questions.e: The adjective 'worthy' is correctly followed by the preposition 'of' to mean deserving. The other options either need a different structure or carry the opposite meaning.
questions.p: Na 'worthy' dey follow 'of' to show say pesin fit do di work. Di oda options no fit join well with 'of'.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the option that best fills the gap.

The committee had debated for hours without reaching an agreement. Just when it seemed the meeting would end in a deadlock, the youngest member proposed an idea so simple yet so effective that it immediately ___ the tension in the room and paved the way for a unanimous decision.
questions.e: The sentence needs a past-tense verb to match 'proposed... that it immediately', so 'dissolved' fits grammatically and in meaning, as it means to make something disappear gradually. The other options are either a noun, an adjective, or the wrong verb form.
questions.p: Di sentence need past-tense verb like 'proposed' to match 'dissolved', so dat e go make sense for grammar.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fills the gap.

The farmers in the drought-stricken region had almost given up hope, but when the rains finally came, their fields turned green ___ , and the harvest that followed was the best in a decade.
questions.e: The word 'again' shows that the fields returned to a former green state after the rain, which matches the hopeful turn of events in the passage. The other options do not logically connect the rain to the greening of the fields.
questions.p: Na 'again' show say di farm come green back as rain fall after dry season. Di oda words no fit di story.

questions.q:
Read the passage and choose the option that best fills the gap.

Before the examination officer could finish explaining the rules, a strange silence fell over the hall. Every candidate sat still, pen in hand, ___ the signal to begin, as if one premature stroke of the pen might cost them the entire paper.
questions.e: The gap needs a present participle to describe an ongoing action happening alongside 'sat still', which fits the pattern of a dangling descriptive phrase modifying the candidates. 'Awaiting' correctly fills this role, while the other forms break the grammatical structure of the sentence.
questions.p: Na 'awaiting' wey be present participle dem need to match how dem sit down dey wait for signal.

questions.q: Identify the grammatical name of the underlined clause: 'Because the market women arrived late, the customers had already left.' (The underlined clause is 'Because the market women arrived late'.)
questions.e: The clause begins with 'Because' and explains why the customers had left, giving a reason. Clauses introduced by 'because' that explain cause are adverbial clauses of reason.
questions.p: Di clause 'Because the market women arrived late' dey show us di reason why di customers leave. Na proper adverbial clause of reason be dat.

questions.q: In the sentence 'What Ngozi said at the meeting surprised everyone,' what is the function of the clause 'What Ngozi said at the meeting'?
o: It is an adjectival clause qualifying 'everyone'
It is an independent clause joined by coordination
It is an adverbial clause of manner
It is a noun clause functioning as the subject
questions.e: The clause 'What Ngozi said at the meeting' acts as the subject of the verb 'surprised', doing the job a noun would do. Clauses that act as subject, object or complement are noun clauses.
questions.p: Dis clause 'What Ngozi said at the meeting' dey stand as di person wey do di work of subject for di sentence. Na correct noun clause be dat.

questions.q: Select the sentence in which 'running' functions as a gerund.
o: The running water flooded the compound
Running every morning keeps Tunde fit
He saw a running tap in the kitchen
The boys were running round the field
questions.e: In this option, 'Running' acts as the subject of the sentence, so it behaves like a noun. A gerund is a verb form ending in -ing that functions as a noun.
questions.p: Na only for option B 'Running' dey play di role of noun as subject of di sentence. Dat one na true gerund.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The man whose car was stolen reported to the police,' what is the grammatical name of 'whose car was stolen'?
questions.e: The clause 'whose car was stolen' gives more information about 'the man', describing him like an adjective would. Clauses beginning with relative pronouns such as 'whose' that qualify a noun are adjectival clauses.
questions.p: Di clause 'whose car was stolen' dey explain more about di man, just like adjective dey do. Na adjectival or relative clause be dat.

questions.q: Read the sentence carefully: 'Having finished her assignment, Blessing decided to visit her aunt in Enugu before it got dark.' What is the grammatical function of 'Having finished her assignment'?
o: It is a noun phrase functioning as object
It is a main clause joined by a conjunction
It is a finite adverbial clause of time
It is a non-finite (participial) phrase functioning adverbially
questions.e: The phrase has no subject of its own and uses a participle 'Having finished', so it is non-finite, not a full clause. It shows the time relationship to the main action, functioning adverbially, like a reduced adverbial clause of time.
questions.p: Dis phrase 'Having finished her assignment' no get subject and e start with participle, so e be non-finite phrase wey dey do adverb work. E correct well well.

questions.q: In the sentence, 'The teacher gave the brilliant student a shiny new trophy,' what is the grammatical function of the phrase 'a shiny new trophy'?
questions.e: The direct object receives the action of the verb 'gave'. 'A shiny new trophy' is the thing given, while 'the brilliant student' is the indirect object who received it.
questions.p: Na direct object be dat because na im receive di action of di verb 'gave'. Wetyn dem give na 'a shiny new trophy', while 'the brilliant student' na di indirect object wey collect am.

questions.q: Identify the grammatical name of the italicised group of words: Chidi, 'the best goalkeeper in the state,' was given an award.
questions.e: The phrase renames Chidi and gives more information about him without using a verb, which is the function of an appositive noun phrase. It is not a clause because it lacks a finite verb.
questions.p: Dis phrase dey rename Chidi and dey give more gist about am without verb. Dat na how noun phrase in apposition dey work.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The committee members disagreed among themselves over the new policy,' what part of speech is 'themselves'?
questions.e: 'Themselves' refers back to 'the committee members' and shows that the action of disagreeing happened within the group itself, which is the role of a reflexive pronoun. It is not emphasising a noun already named for emphasis alone, so it is not intensive here.
questions.p: Di word 'themselves' dey point back to 'the committee members' to show say di disagreement happen among dem. Na reflexive pronoun be dat.

questions.q: Read the sentence: 'The farmer, tired after a long day on the farm, slept early.' What is the grammatical function of 'tired after a long day on the farm'?
o: It functions as the subject of the sentence
It functions as an adverbial clause of reason
It functions as a noun phrase in apposition
It functions as an adjectival phrase modifying 'the farmer'
questions.e: The phrase describes the state of 'the farmer' without containing a finite verb, which is typical of an adjectival (participial) phrase. It answers the question 'what kind of farmer' rather than giving a reason in clause form.
questions.p: Di phrase dey describe how 'the farmer' be, so na adjectival phrase wey dey qualify di farmer. E no get verb inside, na im make am adjective phrase.

questions.q: In the sentence, 'That the governor approved the new salary scale pleased many civil servants,' what is the grammatical function of the clause 'That the governor approved the new salary scale'?
o: It functions as the subject of the sentence
It functions as an adverbial clause of reason
It functions as the object of the verb 'pleased'
It functions as an adjectival clause qualifying 'civil servants'
questions.e: The whole clause acts as a single noun element that performs the action in the sentence, since it is what 'pleased' the civil servants, making it the subject. Many candidates wrongly think it is the object because it comes before the verb, but it is the doer, not the receiver, of the pleasing.
questions.p: Na di whole clause dey do di work of subject here because na im cause di action of di verb 'pleased'. E dey answer wetyn please di civil servants.

questions.q: Study this sentence carefully: 'The woman who sells akara by the roadside, whom everyone in the street respects, trained three nurses.' What is the grammatical name of the clause 'whom everyone in the street respects'?
o: A noun clause functioning as subject
A non-restrictive adjectival clause modifying 'the woman'
questions.e: The clause is set off by commas and adds extra, non-essential information about 'the woman', which is the mark of a non-restrictive adjectival clause. It cannot modify 'akara' because the relative pronoun 'whom' refers only to people, and here it clearly points back to the woman.
questions.p: Di comma dem show say na extra gist wey no too important about di woman dem dey give, and 'whom' dey point to person. Na non-restrictive adjectival clause be dat.
